SERVICE & LICENSING INFORMATION

Service & Licensing Information

Updated: October 4, 2026 · Product information; commercial terms require an executed agreement

Core Principles & Facility Responsibilities

Deterministic Safety

Available checks hold unresolved cases. Physical texture and clinical acceptance still require qualified review.

Data portability review

Confirm export coverage and controlled full-database recovery before facility rollout.

Resident data boundaries

Resident information must remain within facility-approved deployments and processing agreements.

01.Open Core & Commercial Scope

ShorelineOps uses an open core model. Repository license terms govern use of the published software; paid hosting or commercial services require a separate agreement identifying the parties and accepted scope.

This page is product information. It is not an executed Master Services Agreement, subscription contract, or BAA. Current clinical use requires a separate deployment and database for each facility.

See the repository licensing guidance and applicable license files.

02.Clinical Care Responsibilities & Medical Disclaimer

Authorized facility clinicians retain responsibility for diet orders, ingredient assessment, fluid restrictions, and physical texture checks. ShorelineOps provides operational checks and holds unresolved cases; it does not establish that every clinical constraint or meal is safe.

Validate current orders, recipe data, tray holds, and professional review procedures before clinical rollout. Never bypass NPO or allergen holds. Unavailable verification must remain on hold.

03.Proposed Subscriptions & Licensing

The pricing page describes the proposed community, Pro, and Enterprise offerings. Confirm actual availability, facility scope, provider access, billing methods, and accepted commercial terms before subscribing.

Payment processing, cancellation periods, support commitments, and any offline license behavior must be documented in the executed agreement. No unattended purchasing or clinical authority is granted by a subscription tier.

04.Facility Data Ownership & Portability

Facilities must define data ownership, retention, authorized access, export, and termination procedures in the applicable agreement.

The administrator export currently contains selected records; it is not a complete recoverable database image. Full-database backup and controlled restore must be tested separately. JSON, CSV, and SQLite exports are not interchangeable recovery guarantees.

05.Service Level Agreement (SLA) & Offline Resilience

Availability, support response times, recovery targets, and service credits require an executed agreement backed by deployment acceptance. No measured uptime guarantee is represented by this page.

A local installation can operate without internet while devices remain connected to its application server. Disconnected tablets cannot confirm current clinical verification or saved actions, and guaranteed offline mutation replay is not available. Use an approved downtime and reconciliation procedure.

06.Contract Review

Commercial liability allocation and remedies must be reviewed by the contracting parties and stated in their executed agreement. This product information page does not establish a liability cap or replace legal review.

07.Agreement Responsibilities

Governing law and dispute procedures must be established in the applicable executed agreement. No jurisdiction is selected by this informational page.

08.Contact & Legal Notices

Use the contacts identified in the applicable service agreement for formal notices. For product discussion, consult the project repository; do not submit resident information or credentials in public discussions.
